## Structure and components

- [passage] In a regular collection, data is stored sequentially as blocks on disk, optimizing write speed. However, it requires one index for each data point, which quickly grows very large. It also requires a second index that contains the time series identifier and timestamps themselves, so that users can query for a single series. To read this data, MongoDB has to process all of the database and disk blocks that contain it, even if a block only contains a single relevant document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#comparing-time-series-collections-to-regular-collections · keywords: index, time series collection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/
- [passage] Each document you insert should contain a single measurement. To insert multiple documents at once, use the [`db.collection.insertMany()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.insertmany.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.insertMany) method: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-procedures.md#insert-measurements-into-a-time-series-collection · keywords: time series collection, db.collection.insertMany()
- [passage] Before any metadata compaction, the `ESC` and `ECOC` contain one metadata document for every field/value pair of every indexed field. Indexing one encrypted field/value pair across 1000 documents requires 1000 documents in the `ESC` and 1000 documents in the `ECOC`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#storage-costs-for-equality-queryable-fields · keywords: index, working set for time series, ESC, ECOC

- [passage] | Field | Necessity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) | Required | The field to densify. The values of the specified `field` must either be all numeric values or all dates. Documents that do not contain the specified `field` continue through the pipeline unmodified. To specify a `<field>` in an embedded document or in an array, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/document.md#std-label-document-dot-notation) For restrictions, see [`field` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field-restrictions) | | [partitionByFields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-partition-by-fields) | Optional | The set of fields to act as the compound key to group the documents. In the [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) stage, each group of documents is known as a *partition*. If you omit this field, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) uses one partition for the entire collection. For an example, see [Densification with Partitions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-partitions) For restrictions, see [`partitionByFields` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-partition-by-fields-restrictions) | | [range](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-range) | Required | An object that specifies how the data is densified. | | [range.bounds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-bounds) | Required | You can specify `range.bounds` as either: An array: `[ < lower bound >, < upper bound > ]`,; A string: either `"full"` or `"partition"`. If `bounds` is an array: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the range of values within the specified bounds.; The data type for the bounds must correspond to the data type in the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) being densified.; For behavior details, see [`range.bounds` Behavior.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-bounds-behavior) If `bounds` is `"full"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the full range of values of the `field` being densified. If `bounds` is `"partition"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents to each partition, similar to if you had run a `full` range densification on each partition individually. | | [range.step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) | Required | The amount to increment the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) value in each document. [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) creates a new document for each `step` between the existing documents. If [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) is specified, `step` must be an integer. Otherwise, `step` can be any numeric value. | | [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) | Required if [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) is a date. | The unit to apply to the [step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) field when incrementing date values in [field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) You can specify one of the following values for `unit` as a string: `millisecond`; `second`; `minute`; `hour`; `day`; `week`; `month`; `quarter`; `year` For an example, see [Densify Time Series Data.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-time-series) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#syntax · keywords: time series collection, field, <field>, $densify, partitionByFields, range.bounds

## How it works

- [fact] Working set is the subset of data and indexes touched in a typical window, rarely the whole database. Practitioner guidance is to size the cache to working set plus write headroom, and to use a sustained post-warmup page-fault rate as a proxy when the size is unknown. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-cache-undersized-working-set/ · keywords: index, time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [statement] During 8.0 development, Jira SERVER-88316 (fixed in 8.0.0-rc0) showed the server using block processing for a GroupByNull test case with only featureFlagSbeFull set, when the test expected none. This shows the block-processing decision depended on several feature flags. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-88316 · keywords: block processing, time series collection, MongoDB 8.0 Block Processing (time series)
- [passage] - In [time series collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md#std-label-manual-timeseries-collection), documents do not require a unique [\_id](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-_id) field because MongoDB does not create an index on the `_id` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#properties-of-time-series-data · keywords: index, time series collection, _id
- [passage] In time series collections, documents do not require a unique _id field because MongoDB does not create an index on the _id field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ · keywords: index, time series collection

- [passage] When migrating or backfilling into a time series collection, always insert the documents in order, from oldest to newest. In this case, [`mongodump`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongodump) exports documents in natural order and the `--maintainInsertionOrder` option for [`mongorestore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongorestore) guarantees the same insertion order for documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-migrate-with-tools.md#steps · keywords: time series collection, mongodump, --maintainInsertionOrder, mongorestore

Writes are organized so that data from the same source is stored alongside other data points from a similar point in time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md#time-series-collections · keywords: time series collection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections/

- [passage] Use the following pages to create and configure your time series collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-create-configure.md · keywords: time series collection
- [passage] Use this tutorial to shard a new or existing time series collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-shard-collection.md · keywords: time series collection

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A MongoDB staff forum answer (March 2022) gave an informal rule of thumb of RAM at 15-20% of total data size, covering indexes, working set, queries and OS. It is not an official time-series formula and cites MongoDB 4.0 docs. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/working-set-should-be-sized-to-fit-into-ram-or-wiredtiger-internal-cache/140684 · keywords: index, time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [statement] A forum report with indexes on t/c in both directions shows a range filter { c: x, t: { $lte: ... } } with sort { t: -1 } spending IXSCAN ~4s but FETCH ~2-5 minutes, while a similar $gte ascending query took ~1s; no answer was given, version unstated. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/filter-on-time-series-with-lte-on-timestamp-and-reverse-index-is-too-slow/296074 · keywords: index, time series collection, Time-Series Sort and Range Query Patterns
- [passage] The maximum size for documents within a time series collection is 4 MB. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#document-size · keywords: time series collection

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] MongoDB automatically enables block processing for eligible time series queries. You cannot manually specify whether a query uses block processing. To see if your time series query uses block processing, see [`stages`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.winningPlan.slotBasedPlan.stages) in the explain plan output. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying.md#block-processing · keywords: block processing, index, time series collection, time series query, stages
- [fact] To check whether a query used block processing, inspect explain output at queryPlanner.winningPlan.slotBasedPlan.stages. A slotBasedPlan field means SBE ran the query. Slow-query logs carry a queryFramework field with value sbe or classic. The docs show no example of what block-processing stages look like. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.2/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying/ · keywords: block processing, index, time series collection, MongoDB 8.0 Block Processing (time series)
- [fact] Block processing is automatic. Users cannot enable or disable it for a single query. Eligibility is decided per query, and queries with unsupported operators or expressions run on the classic engine. SBE support is version specific and still changing. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.2/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying/ · keywords: block processing, time series collection, MongoDB 8.0 Block Processing (time series)
- [fact] Default WiredTiger internal cache is the larger of 50% of (RAM - 1 GB) or 256 MB. MongoDB advises against raising it above the default, and in containers it must be set below the container's RAM limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/storage/ · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [statement] Undersized-cache signals per one monitoring vendor: sustained fill above ~80% with rising eviction rates, dirty ratio above 15% (warning) or 20% (critical), and application-thread evictions. These thresholds are vendor heuristics, not MongoDB documentation. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-cache-undersized-working-set/ · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [passage] You cannot run sharding administration commands on sharded time series collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#sharding-administration-commands · keywords: time series collection, time series sharding
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `distanceField` | string | The output field that contains the calculated distance. To specify a field within an embedded document, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation) This field is required for queries on timeseries collections. Starting in MongoDB 8.1, `distanceField` is optional for queries on non-timeseries collections. | | `distanceMultiplier` | number | Optional. The factor to multiply all distances returned by the query. For example, use the `distanceMultiplier` to convert radians, as returned by a spherical query, to kilometers by multiplying by the radius of the Earth. | | `includeLocs` | string | Optional. This specifies the output field that identifies the location used to calculate the distance. This option is useful when a location field contains multiple locations. To specify a field within an embedded document, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation) | | `key` | | Optional. Specify the geospatial indexed field to use when calculating the distance. If your collection has multiple `2d` and/or multiple `2dsphere` indexes, you **must** use the `key` option to specify the indexed field path to use. [Specify Which Geospatial Index to Use](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geonear.md#std-label-pipeline-geoNear-key-param-example) provides a full example. If there is more than one `2d` index or more than one `2dsphere` index and you do not specify a `key`, MongoDB will return an error. If you do not specify the `key`, and you have at most only one `2d` index and/or only one `2dsphere` index, MongoDB looks first for a `2d` index to use. If a `2d` index does not exists, then MongoDB looks for a `2dsphere` index to use. You must specify the `key` field for `$geoNear` on a time series collection. | | `maxDistance` | number | Optional. The maximum distance from the center point that the documents *can* be. MongoDB limits the results to those documents that fall within the specified distance from the center point. Starting in version 7.2, you can specify a valid constant [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to a number. Specify the distance in meters if the specified point is [GeoJSON](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-GeoJSON) and in radians if the specified point is [legacy coordinate pairs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-legacy-coordinate-pairs) | | `minDistance` | number | Optional. The minimum distance from the center point that the documents *can* be. MongoDB limits the results to those documents that fall outside the specified distance from the center point. Starting in version 7.2, you can specify a valid constant [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to a number. Specify the distance in meters for GeoJSON data and in radians for legacy coordinate pairs. | | `near` | GeoJSON point or [legacy coordinate pair](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-legacy-coordinate-pairs) | The point for which to find the closest documents. If using a [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index, you can specify the point as either a GeoJSON point or legacy coordinate pair. If using a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) index, specify the point as a legacy coordinate pair. | | `query` | document | Optional. Limits the results to the documents that match the query. The query syntax is the usual MongoDB [read operation query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#std-label-read-operations-query-argument) syntax. You cannot specify a [`$near`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near.md#mongodb-query-op.-near) predicate in the `query` field of the `$geoNear` stage. You can't use the `query` field for `$geoNear` on a [time series collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md#std-label-manual-timeseries-landing) | | `spherical` | boolean | Optional. Determines how MongoDB calculates the distance between two points: When `true`, MongoDB uses [`$nearSphere`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nearsphere.md#mongodb-query-op.-nearSphere) semantics and calculates distances using spherical geometry.; When `false`, MongoDB uses [`$near`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near.md#mongodb-query-op.-near) semantics: spherical geometry for [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) indexes and planar geometry for [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) indexes. *Default: false.* | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.md#definition · keywords: index, time series collection, distanceField, distanceMultiplier, includeLocs, key
- [passage] For time series collections, TTL indexes also remove a bucket of data when all documents inside it expire. This is equal to the upper timestamp limit of the bucket, plus the `expireAfterSeconds` value. For example, if a bucket covers data up until `2023-03-27T18:29:59Z` and `expireAfterSeconds` is 300, the TTL index expires the bucket after `2023-03-27T18:34:59Z`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl.md#expiration-of-data · keywords: index, time series collection, expireAfterSeconds, 2023-03-27T18:29:59Z, 2023-03-27T18:34:59Z · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/
- [passage] Ensure that you run the `mongorestore` command with the [`--noIndexRestore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md#std-option-mongorestore.--noIndexRestore) option. `mongorestore` cannot create indexes on time series collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-migrate-with-tools.md#steps · keywords: index, time series collection, mongorestore, --noIndexRestore
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, creating an index with the name of `"_id_"` or specifying a hint of `"_id_"` on time series collections returns an error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#hint-on-id-index · keywords: index, time series collection, "_id_"
- [passage] If you specify a modification in the `timeseries` parameter of your `collMod` operation, you cannot use other modification options in the same command. You must perform time series modifications in a dedicated command that is separate from other collection modifications. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#modify-time-series-collections · keywords: time series collection, timeseries, collMod
- [passage] If MongoDB cannot obtain the sort order with an index scan, then MongoDB uses a top-k sort algorithm. This algorithm buffers the first `k` results (or last, depending on the sort order) seen so far by the underlying index or collection access. If the memory footprint of these `k` results exceeds 100 megabytes, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) with a value of `false` (in which case, the query fails). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#limit-results · keywords: index, working set for time series, cursor.allowDiskUse(), false
- [passage] Limits the amount of memory that simultaneous [index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) on one collection may consume for their duration. The specified amount of memory is shared between all indexes built using a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command or its shell helper [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes). Increasing the limit may avoid negative performance impacts in some cases, such as when building numerous indexes simultaneously with a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command and/or when working with index key data set sizes that exceed 500GB. The memory consumed by an index build is separate from the WiredTiger cache memory (see [`cacheSizeGB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB)). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, working set for time series, createIndexes, db.collection.createIndexes(), cacheSizeGB
- [passage] Rolling indexes build indexes on the applicable nodes sequentially and may reduce the performance impact of an index build if your deployment's average CPU utilization exceeds (N-1)/N-10% where N is the number of CPU threads available to mongod of if the WiredTiger cache fill ratio regularly exceeds 90%. If your deployment does not meet this criteria, use the default index build. You can't create a rolling index on an M0 free cluster or M2/M5 shared cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-rollingIndex.md · keywords: index, working set for time series
- [passage] You can't use the `query` field for `$geoNear` on a [time series collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md#std-label-manual-timeseries-landing) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-aggregations-operators.md#geonear · keywords: time series collection, query, $geoNear · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md
- [passage] You cannot use the [`$merge`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-merge) aggregation stage to add data from another collection to a time series collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-aggregations-operators.md#merge · keywords: time series collection, $merge · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md
- [passage] | `$out` | [`$merge`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-merge) | | --- | --- | | Can output to a collection in the same or different database. | Can output to a collection in the same or different database. | | Creates a new collection if the output collection does not already exist. | Creates a new collection if the output collection does not already exist. | | Replaces the output collection completely if it already exists. | Can incorporate results (insert new documents, merge documents, replace documents, keep existing documents, fail the operation, process documents with a custom update pipeline) into an existing collection.Can replace the content of the collection but only if the aggregation results contain a match for all existing documents in the collection. | | Cannot output to a sharded collection. Input collection, however, can be sharded. | Can output to a sharded collection. Input collection can also be sharded. | | Starting in MongoDB 7.0.3 and 7.1, can output to a time series collection. | Cannot output to a time series collection. | | Corresponds to the SQL statements:`INSERT INTO T2 SELECT * FROM T1`; `SELECT * INTO T2 FROM T1` | Corresponds to the SQL statement:`MERGE T2 AS TARGET USING (SELECT * FROM T1) AS SOURCE ON MATCH (T2.ID = SOURCE.ID) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET TARGET.FIELDX = SOURCE.FIELDY WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (FIELDX) VALUES (SOURCE.FIELDY)`; Create/Refresh Materialized Views | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/out.md#comparison-with-merge · keywords: time series collection, $out, $merge, INSERT INTO T2 SELECT * FROM T1, SELECT * INTO T2 FROM T1 · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md
- [passage] You cannot create a time series collection as a [capped collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/capped-collections.md#std-label-manual-capped-collection) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#capped-collections · keywords: time series collection
- [passage] - You cannot convert an existing collection into a time series collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#modification-of-collection-type · keywords: time series collection
- [passage] - You cannot convert a time series collection into a different collection type. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#modification-of-collection-type · keywords: time series collection
- [passage] You cannot write to time series collections in [transactions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#transactions · keywords: time series collection
- [passage] If the time between the end of the to-be-rolledback instance's oplog and the first operation after the common point (the last point where the source node and the to-be-rolledback node had the same data) exceeds this value, the rollback will fail. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#replication-and-consistency · keywords: time series query

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB's blog (published 2024-12-09, updated 2025-07-21) claims 10-40x improvements across workloads, up to 100x for some large aggregations, and 20x ops/sec versus 7.0 in a worked example. The example ran on an Atlas M50 using MongoDB's TSBS fork: about 6 million events, a 24-hour $match, $sort, $group with $dateTrunc, $setWindowFields and $expMovingAvg. — https://mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/key-enhancements-mongodb-8-0-block-processing · keywords: block processing, time series collection, time series query, MongoDB 8.0 Block Processing (time series)
- [passage] Delta Encoding takes advantage of the data in your time series collection having time-series characteristics. Instead of storing absolute values, Delta Encoding assumes that the measurements will not change rapidly between each other. This approach reduces the amount of information required by only storing the difference between measurements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-compression.md#delta-encoding-delta-compression · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series
- [passage] Starting in version 8.0, MongoDB may execute certain time series queries using block processing. This performance improvement processes queries in "blocks" of data, rather than individual values. Block processing improves query execution speed and throughput when working with time series collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying.md#block-processing · keywords: block processing, time series collection · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.2/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying/
- [passage] Time series collections use [zstd](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-zstd) compression, which differs from the global default compression algorithm, [snappy.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-snappy) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-compression.md#default-compression-algorithm · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series
- [passage] MongoDB does not create an index on the `_id` field when you create a time series collection. This differs from regular collections which have an index on the `_id` field by default. Commands that specify a hint on the `_id` field on time series collections return an error unless you manually create an index on the `_id` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#default-index · keywords: index, time series collection, _id
- [fact] Allegro's 5.0.3 benchmark found aggregation over a random six-hour window 23-48% faster on a time series collection than a regular one (10K to 100K queries), but single-timestamp lookups were nearly equal (16.854s vs 16.038s for 1M queries). — https://blog.allegro.tech/2021/12/performance-evaluation-of-timeseries.html · keywords: time series collection, Time-Series Sort and Range Query Patterns

## Facts and statements

- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, if a query uses [block processing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying.md#std-label-timeseries-querying-block-processing), `block_to_row` and `ts_bucket_to_cellblock` appear in the `stages` output. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: block processing, index, time series collection, block_to_row, ts_bucket_to_cellblock, stages · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [statement] The SBE reference page says SBE is disabled automatically on collections that have an index with a hashed-field prefix followed by a non-hashed field, with both fields in the index. Ineligible queries fall back to the classic engine. The page does not tie this rule to time series specifically. — https://mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/sbe · keywords: block processing, index, time series collection, MongoDB 8.0 Block Processing (time series)
- [fact] Collection data in the WiredTiger cache is uncompressed, so block compression saves disk but not cache space; the OS filesystem cache holds the compressed on-disk form. Indexes in cache still benefit from prefix compression. Compressed time series storage size therefore understates the cache footprint of hot buckets. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/storage/ · keywords: index, time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [fact] MongoDB's docs state a bucket holds at most 1000 measurements or 125 KiB, whichever is lower, and MongoDB may enforce a lower maximum for high-cardinality data so the working set of buckets fits in the WiredTiger cache. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series, Working Set Sizing for Time Series
- [passage] Connect [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) for your sharded cluster. Specify the `host` and `port` on which the `mongos` is running: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-shard-collection.md#create-a-sharded-time-series-collection · keywords: time series collection, time series sharding, mongosh, mongos, host, port
- [passage] - Shards a new time series collection named `weather` on the `test` database. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-shard-collection.md#create-a-sharded-time-series-collection · keywords: time series collection, time series sharding, weather, test
- [passage] This page describes how MongoDB compresses data in time series collections, and how you can optimize compression. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-compression.md · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.2, time series collections use **column compression**. Column compression adds a number of innovations that work together to significantly improve practical compression, reduce your data's overall storage on disk, and improve read performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-compression.md#column-compression · keywords: time series collection, working set for time series

- [passage] | Number | Description | | --- | --- | | 0 | Generic binary subtype | | 1 | Function data | | 2 | Binary (old) | | 3 | UUID (old) | | 4 | UUID | | 5 | MD5 | | 6 | Encrypted BSON value | | 7 | Compressed time series data **New in version 5.2** | | 8 | Sensitive data, such as a key or secret. MongoDB does not log literal values for binary data with subtype 8. Instead, MongoDB logs a placeholder value of `###`. | | 9 | Vector data, which is densely packed arrays of numbers of the same type. | | 128 | Custom data | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/convert.md#binary-subtypes · keywords: time series collection, ###

- [passage] - A string other than `week`, [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses a reference date of `2000-01-01T00:00:00.00Z`. For example, if [binSize](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-binSize) is `10` and [unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-unit) is `year`, example time periods are: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateTrunc.md#binsize-and-unit-fields · keywords: time series query, week, $dateTrunc, 2000-01-01T00:00:00.00Z, 10, year
- [passage] - Equal to `week`, [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses a reference date that is set to the earliest first day of the week that is greater than or equal to `2000-01-01`. The first day is set using [startOfWeek](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-startOfWeek) (the default is Sunday). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateTrunc.md#binsize-and-unit-fields · keywords: time series query, week, $dateTrunc, 2000-01-01
